statement: The system shall let participating agencies exchange a common view of traffic conditions, incidents, and field-device status despite differences in their internal systems.
The system's data shall be timely, reliable, and usable across agencies without manual re-entry or hand translation.
The network shall let authorized agencies coordinate roadside devices in a controlled way.
The network shall allow management of message signs and other connected field equipment across jurisdictional boundaries when needed.

Organizations without a full traffic management center shall be able to access a simple map-based view of current traffic information and participate in the network without needing their own full operations center.
The network should use an established transportation data standard where possible rather than a custom format.
The data standard or format used by the network must support traffic conditions consistently enough for agencies to exchange them reliably.
The data standard or format used by the network must support incidents consistently enough for agencies to exchange them reliably.
The data standard or format used by the network must support device status consistently enough for agencies to exchange them reliably.
Network access must be role-based and agency-specific.
The network must apply stronger access controls for anything that can change roadside devices.
Users and systems must be authenticated before they can view or publish data.
Only specifically authorized agencies or operators may issue control commands.
Field-device control must include extra logging and approval rules.

The system shall support agencies that need to coordinate responses.
